e-562.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Given By a Polynomial
e-562.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\textrm m / \textrm s^2,$ given by the function $a(t) = 4t^2 - 3t^3,$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\textrm m / \textrm s$ when $t=0 \,\textrm s,$ calculate the velocity (in $\textrm m / \textrm s$) of the particle at time $t.$
e-562.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (4{t}^{2}-3{t}^{3})\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{t}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0) = 2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{4}{3}(0)^{3}-\frac{3}{4}(0)^{4}+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t) = \dfrac{4}{3}t^3 -\dfrac{3}{4}t^4 + 2.$

e-563.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Not a Polynomial
e-563.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\textrm m / \textrm s^2,$ given by the function $a(t) =2e^{-t}+6t^2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-4 \,\textrm m / \textrm s$ when $t=0 \,\textrm s,$ calculate the speed of the particle at the moment  $t=1\,\textrm{s}.$
e-563.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2{e}^{-t}+6{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2(-{e}^{-t})+\frac{6}{3}{t}^{3}+C \\  & =-2{e}^{-t}+2{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0) = -4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =-2{e}^{-0}+2\cdot {0}^{3}+C \\ -4 & =-2+0+C \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t) = -2  e^{-t}+ 2t^3 -2.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=1\,\textrm{s}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =-2{e}^{-1}+2(1)^{3}-2 \\  & =-2{e}^{-1}+2-2 \\  & =-\frac{2}{e}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\dfrac 2 e\,\textrm{m/s}.$

decision.explanation: Integrating acceleration gives v(t)=2t^3-t^4+C. Since v(2)=16-16+C=-5, C=-5. Thus option d is correct.

If the particle has velocity $v=-5\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=2\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{ft/s}$) of the particle at time $t.$

$$

$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(2)=-5.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-5 & =2(2)^{3}-(2)^{4}+C \\ -5 & =16-16+C \\ C & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

If the particle has velocity $v=-5\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=2\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{ft/s}$) of the particle at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (6{t}^{2}-4{t}^{3})\text{d}t \\  & =2{t}^{3}-{t}^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(2)=-5.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-5 & =2(2)^{3}-(2)^{4}+C \\ -5 & =16-16+C \\ C & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2{t}^{3}-{t}^{4}-5.$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3+8t-3{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-1\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3+8t-3{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =3t+4{t}^{2}-{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =3(0)+4(0)^{2}-(0)^{3}+C \\ -1 & =0+C \\ C & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3t+4{t}^{2}-{t}^{3}-1.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =3(2)+4(2)^{2}-(2)^{3}-1 \\  & =6+16-8-1 \\  & =13\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $13\,\text{m/s}.$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=\sqrt{{t}^{3}},$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=0\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=1\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \sqrt{{t}^{3}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {t}^{3/2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{2}{5}{t}^{5/2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =\frac{2}{5}(0)^{5/2}+C \\ 0 & =0+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{2}{5}{t}^{5/2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=1\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =\frac{2}{5}(1)^{5/2}=\frac{2}{5}\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\frac{2}{5}\,\text{m/s}.$

Question 9

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in ft/s2, given by the function a(t)=4sin⁡(2t), where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=3ft/s when t=π4s, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment t=π2s.

a
 4ft/s
b
 1ft/s
c
 3ft/s
d
 5ft/s
e
 7ft/s
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫4sin⁡(2t)dt=4(−12cos⁡(2t))+C=−2cos⁡(2t)+C. To determine C, we use the fact that v(π4)=3. Substituting this into the above gives 3=−2cos⁡(2⋅π4)+C3=−2cos⁡(π2)+C3=−2⋅0+CC=3. Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=3−2cos⁡(2t).

We evaluate the velocity at time t=π2s: v(π2)=3−2cos⁡(2⋅π2)=3−2cos⁡(π)=3−2⋅(−1)=5ft/s.

Finally, since the speed is equal to |v(t)|, we conclude that the speed of the particle is 5ft/s.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Not a Polynomial
content.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{ft}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=3\,\text{ft}/\text{s}$ when $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=\frac{\pi }{2}\,\text{s}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =4(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))+C \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(\frac{\pi }{4})=3.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})+C \\ 3 & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+C \\ 3 & =-2\cdot 0+C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\frac{\pi }{2}\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =3-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =3-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =3-2\cdot (-1) \\  & =5\,\text{ft}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $5\,\text{ft}/\text{s}.$

after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=9{e}^{-3t}-4{e}^{-t}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=1\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (9{e}^{-3t}-4{e}^{-t})\,\text{d}t \\  & =9(-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t})-4(-{e}^{-t})+C \\  & =-3{e}^{-3t}+4{e}^{-t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-3{e}^{0}+4{e}^{0}+C \\ 1 & =-3+4+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=4{e}^{-t}-3{e}^{-3t}.$
